ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Know whether a page is live before I publish
ux.finding: Every page the user creates wears a 'Draft' badge and every one of them is published. The panel defaults a page with no visibility set to 'draft'; the exporter treats exactly that state as live and ships it, and the Publish panel counts it among the pages that will deploy. So the only signal the panel gives about what will go live is wrong for every page nobody has opened Advanced settings on — which is all of them.
ux.evidence: usePages.ts:120 (status = settings.visibility ?? 'draft'); engine/export/ExportEngine.ts:120-122 isPageLive returns true when visibility is undefined; publish/usePublishSnapshot.ts:172 counts pages by isPageLive. Searched: 'visibility', 'isPageLive', 'draft', 'PageStatus'.
ux.fix: Badge the row from the same predicate the deploy uses. If a page really has no publication state, say 'Will publish' rather than inventing a Draft that does not exist, and put the per-page publish decision on the row instead of three clicks deep in a modal's Advanced tab.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Keep a page out of the next publish while I finish it
ux.finding: There is no way to put a page into Draft. The visibility control offers Live / Hidden / Password only, while the panel's own status vocabulary declares draft, scheduled, external and error. So the badge on every new row names a state the user can neither reach, leave, nor verify, and 'stop this page shipping' has to be spelled as 'Hidden', which the same screen says means something else.
ux.evidence: page-settings/AdvancedTab.tsx:24 renders exactly ['live','hidden','password']; types.ts:9 PageStatus declares seven values; utils/statusLabel.ts:12-20 has labels for all seven. Searched: 'draft', 'visibility', 'PageStatus', 'scheduled', 'setVisibility'.
ux.fix: Either add Draft as a first-class visibility with a row action ('Unpublish' / 'Publish this page'), or delete the four statuses nothing writes so the badge only ever shows a state the user chose.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Fix a typo in my meta description
ux.finding: Opening page settings and changing one unrelated field silently publishes the page. The drawer reads any page that is not hidden or password-protected as 'live', and every save writes that value back — so editing the SEO title on a page badged Draft flips it to Live, with no control on screen having said so and no confirmation.
ux.evidence: page-settings/usePageSettings.ts:103-104 (visibility = password ? 'password' : hidden ? 'hidden' : 'live'); :267-284 save() always writes settings.visibility. Searched: 'visibility', 'getPersistedState', 'updatePage'.
ux.fix: Do not write a field the user did not touch. Seed visibility as 'unset' and only persist it when the Advanced control is used.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Delete a page I no longer need
ux.finding: The delete confirmation never says what else breaks. Internal links are stored as a page id, and the exporter silently rewrites any link whose page is gone to the home page. So deleting 'Pricing' turns every 'See pricing' button on the site into a link to Home, and the user finds out on the published site. The dialog says only 'This page and everything on it is removed.'
ux.evidence: PagesTab.tsx:329 confirm copy; inspector/sections/LinkSection.tsx:191 writes '#page:<id>'; engine/export/ExportEngine.ts:801-802 falls back to 'index.html' for an unresolvable id. Searched: '#page:', 'pageHrefs', 'internal link'.
ux.fix: Count inbound links before the dialog opens and name them ('3 links on 2 pages point here'), with the option to see them. After deleting, leave those links visibly broken rather than silently re-pointing them at Home.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Know which page visitors land on
ux.finding: On a site where nobody has explicitly chosen a homepage, the homepage is whichever row happens to sit first — and no row shows the home glyph, so the panel looks like a site with no homepage at all. Dragging a page to the top changes what the site serves at its root; deleting the first page does the same. Neither action warns, and the delete guard that is supposed to protect the homepage never fires because no page is flagged.
ux.evidence: engine/elements/manager/PageManager.ts:243 is the only writer of isHome (the explicit 'Set as homepage'); createPage (:61-93) never sets it; engine/export/ExportEngine.ts:146 falls back to pages[0]; PageRow.tsx:231 draws the roof glyph only when page.isHome. Searched: 'isHome', 'setHomePage', 'homepage', 'index.html'.
ux.fix: Flag the first page as home at creation, or show the row that is acting as the homepage with an explicit 'Homepage (by position)' marker so reorder and delete can warn before they change it.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Give a page a URL that another page already uses
ux.finding: Typing a slug that clashes with another page starts a toast that will not stop. The form autosaves half a second after any change; the save refuses because of the slug error and raises a warning toast; the toast re-renders the form, which restarts the autosave timer, which refuses and toasts again — roughly every half second, forever, until the slug is fixed or the modal is closed. The same loop runs after choosing Password visibility before typing a password, and after typing an unclosed tag in the head-code box.
ux.evidence: page-settings/PageSettingsDrawer.tsx:41-45 (autosave effect, dependency array includes `s`, a fresh object every render); usePageSettings.ts:248-251 (slug refusal + toast), :258-261 (password refusal + toast), :252-257 (head-code refusal + toast); chrome-ui/Toast.tsx:151-153 the provider memo changes on every toast so every useToast consumer re-renders. Searched: 'isDirty', 'setTimeout(', 'addToast', 'ToastContext'.
ux.fix: Do not autosave into a known-invalid state at all — show the error beside the field (it already is) and hold the save until it clears, with no toast. Only a save the user asked for should ever be able to speak.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Add a page after deleting one
ux.finding: '+ Add page' can create a second page with the same name AND the same URL as an existing one. The default name is 'Page {count+1}', so on a site of Home / About / Page 3, deleting About and adding a page produces a second 'Page 3' at /page-3. The panel refuses a duplicate name when you RENAME a page, and applies no check at all when it creates one; two identical rows appear, both claiming the same address.
ux.evidence: shared/utils/pageUtils.ts:16-20 getDefaultPageName; usePages.ts:176-198 addPage passes the name and slugified slug straight through; engine/elements/manager/PageManager.ts:61-93 createPage performs no name or slug uniqueness check; the only duplicate check is PagesTab.tsx:99-105, on rename only. Searched: 'getDefaultPageName', 'existingSlugs', 'isSlugDuplicate', 'createPage('. (Re-verified prior claim MOD-B-03 — still true at HEAD.)
ux.fix: Make the create path use the same uniqueness helpers the duplicate path already has (uniqueCopyName / uniqueCopySlug, PageManager.ts:460-475), and name new pages after what they are rather than a counter.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Add a page and have visitors be able to find it
ux.finding: Adding a page does not add it to the site's navigation, and the product offers no way to do it in bulk. The navbar is a static block of hard-coded links labelled Home / About / Services / Contact, every one of them pointing at '#' until someone wires it by hand element by element in the inspector. Nothing generates navigation from the page list — the page list has no consumer that produces links at all. So the 'Set as homepage' toast that warns 'your navigation menu may need updating manually' is telling the truth, and the manual work it names has no tool behind it.
ux.evidence: blocks/Sections/Navbar.tsx:17 the navbar block's content is a fixed HTML string with four href="#" links; inspector/sections/LinkSection.tsx:191 is the only place a page becomes a link, one element at a time; usePages.ts:308-312 the homepage toast. Every consumer of getAllPages() is a panel, the exporter, recovery or templates — none builds navigation. Searched: 'navigation', 'navMenu', 'SiteNav', 'menuBuilder', 'navbar', and enumerated all getAllPages() callers.
ux.fix: Either generate the primary navigation from the page list (with a per-page 'show in nav' toggle in the Pages panel), or make the page-to-link relationship visible so the user can see which pages nothing links to.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Reorder my pages
ux.finding: Dragging a page shows the user nothing. No insertion line, no highlighted target row, no ghost — the row simply jumps to a new position when the mouse is released, and if the drop lands somewhere unexpected there is no way to have known. A drop indicator element is rendered on every list but the class that makes it visible is never applied by anything.
ux.evidence: PagesTab.css:319 '.bd-pg-drop-indicator.show { display: block; }'; the element is rendered at PageList.tsx:155 and :351 and no code adds 'show'; PageRow.tsx:115-119 dragover sets only dropEffect, no class. Searched: 'show', 'classList', 'dragover', 'drop-indicator', 'isDragOver' (which exists only on PageFolder.tsx:66).
ux.fix: Draw the insertion line at the computed drop position during dragover, and highlight the row being displaced.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Move a page to the top of the list
ux.finding: No drag can put a page in first position. Every drop inserts the dragged page AFTER the row it landed on, so the top slot is unreachable — and on a site with no explicit homepage the top slot is the homepage. The engine supports prepending; no part of the UI ever asks for it.
ux.evidence: PageList.tsx:313-315 always calls reorderPage(draggedId, page.id); PageManager.reorderPage:337-343 supports afterId === null as prepend, and no caller passes null. Searched: 'reorderPage', 'afterId', 'prepend'.
ux.fix: Make the drop position depend on where in the row the pointer is (above the midpoint inserts before), so the first slot is reachable.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Rename 'Page 3' to 'Pricing'
ux.finding: Renaming a page never changes its URL and nothing says so. A page created as 'Page 3' and renamed to 'Pricing' stays at /page-3 forever unless the user separately opens page settings and edits the slug. The SEO panel then marks that same URL down as a numbered placeholder — the product penalises the user for a URL its own rename flow refused to update.
ux.evidence: usePages.ts:213-222 commitRename writes only { name: trimmed }; utils/seoScore.ts:24 isPlaceholderSlug flags /^page-\d+$/ and the score withholds 10 points for it; page-settings/usePageSettings.ts:264-269 is the only path that writes a slug. Searched: 'commitRename', 'slugManuallySet', 'updatePage(.*slug', 'normalizeSlug'.
ux.fix: At rename, offer the matching slug inline ('also change the URL to /pricing?') for any page whose slug was never hand-edited, which the engine already tracks as slugManuallySet.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Rename a page from the tab bar under the canvas
ux.finding: The rename popover under the canvas tab shows the URL the page will have, and then does not write it. Type 'Pricing' and the popover reads '/pricing'; submit and the page keeps its old address. The one place in the product that shows a user the URL consequence of a rename is the one place that is lying about it.
ux.evidence: shell/PageTabBar.tsx:64-74 computes nameValidation.slug via normalizeSlug(editName); :328-332 renders '/{slug}' in the popover; :139-145 handleRenameSubmit calls updatePage(id, { name }) only. Searched: 'nameValidation', 'normalizeSlug', 'handleRenameSubmit'.
ux.fix: Either write the slug the popover promises (for pages whose slug was never hand-edited), or stop drawing a URL the submit will not produce.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Delete five pages at once
ux.finding: Deleting five selected pages fires five separate toasts, each naming one page and each carrying its own 'Undo' — and every one of those Undo buttons undoes all five, because the whole loop lands in one history entry. The confirm dialog correctly says one undo brings them all back; the five toasts that follow it say the opposite five times over.
ux.evidence: PagesTab.tsx:188-192 confirmBulkDelete loops p.deletePage; usePages.ts:279-289 each call raises a toast with an Undo action; chrome-ui/Toast.tsx:88-92 the store has no cap and no dedupe; PagesTab.tsx:345-347 the dialog copy promises a single undo. Searched: 'addToast', 'deletePage', 'MAX', 'dedupe'.
ux.fix: One toast for one user action: '5 pages deleted · Undo'. The per-page toast belongs to the per-page delete.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Duplicate several pages at once
ux.finding: Bulk duplicate reports nothing at all. The selection clears, five copies are appended to the bottom of a list that may be scrolled elsewhere, and the user gets no toast, no scroll to the new rows and no selection of them — the only evidence the action worked is finding the copies by hand. The single-page duplicate is equally silent; it speaks only when it fails.
ux.evidence: PagesTab.tsx:151-154 handleBulkDuplicate loops duplicatePage then clears selection; usePages.ts:228-254 duplicatePage toasts only in the failure and catch branches. Searched: 'duplicatePage', 'addToast', 'scrollIntoView'.
ux.fix: Confirm the outcome and put the user next to it: toast the count, select the new copies, scroll the first one into view.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Finish editing page settings and get back to my page
ux.finding: The page settings modal has no visible way out. It is a 580x520 card on a dark scrim carrying a title, three tabs and a form — no close control, and because it autosaves there is no Save or Done button either. The only exits are the Escape key and clicking the dark area outside, neither of which is labelled anywhere on screen.
ux.evidence: page-settings/PageSettingsDrawer.tsx docstring line 8 ('There is no X'), :84-142 renders scrim + dialog with no close button; PagesTab.css:562-576 fixed 580x520 centred card. Searched: 'onClose', 'aria-label="Close"', 'CloseButton', 'X'.
ux.fix: Give the modal a labelled exit. An autosaving form still needs a 'Done' the user can aim at.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Manage pages
ux.finding: Two page managers ship side by side and disagree. The tab bar under the canvas does rename, duplicate, set-as-home and delete; the Pages panel does those plus settings, copy link, reorder, folders and bulk actions. When only one page exists the tab bar HIDES Delete and the panel DISABLES it with an explanatory tooltip. 'Set as home' from the tab bar skips the external-page guard and the 'your navigation menu may need updating' warning the panel raises for the identical action. The two delete confirmations use different wording for the same consequence.
ux.evidence: shell/PageTabBar.tsx:385-414 (menu), :406 hides Delete when pages.length <= 1, :207-210 handleSetHome with no guard and no toast, :424 confirm copy; PageContextMenu.tsx:99-106 disables Delete with a tooltip; usePages.ts:294-324 setHomepage with the external guard and the navigation warning; PagesTab.tsx:329 the other confirm copy. Searched: 'PageTabBar', 'setHomePage', 'ConfirmDialog'.
ux.fix: One page-actions menu, used by both surfaces. Decide once whether an unavailable action is hidden or disabled-with-a-reason, and use the same delete copy in both places.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Change a published page's URL without losing its traffic
ux.finding: At the exact moment the product knows both the old URL and the new one, it tells the user to go and set up a redirect 'in your hosting settings' — while the editor itself ships a Redirects screen two panels away. The engine already records the previous slug on every change and nothing reads it. So the user leaves the product to do by hand something the product could have offered as one button.
ux.evidence: page-settings/SeoTab.tsx:252-253 warning copy; settings/SettingsTab.tsx:87 the shipped 'Redirects — 301 / 302 + 404 suggester' row; settings/screens/RedirectsScreen.tsx:62-142 a manual from/to form (no 404 suggester in it); PageManager.ts:133-141 writes slugHistory that nothing consumes. Searched: 'redirect', 'slugHistory', '301'.
ux.fix: Replace the copy with an action: 'Add a 301 from /old to /new' that writes the redirect, pre-filled from the change that is happening.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Organise 30 pages into folders
ux.finding: Folders look like part of the site and live in one browser. They are stored in local browser storage, never in the project, so they vanish on another device, are invisible to a teammate and disappear when site data is cleared — and nothing on screen says so. Deleting a folder is one unconfirmed click on a small icon, and it is outside undo: the panel's own delete-page copy promises that Cmd-Z brings things back, and for a folder it does not.
ux.evidence: useFolders.ts:24-60 localStorage key 'pg-folders-v1-<siteId>', :140-145 deleteFolder with no confirm; PageFolder.tsx:243-256 the delete IconButton fires onFolderDelete directly; nothing writes folders into ProjectData. Searched: 'folders', 'pg-folders', 'localStorage', 'FolderItem'. (Confirms prior claim MOD-B-09.)
ux.fix: Either persist folders with the project, or label them plainly as a private view ('Folders are yours only, on this browser'). Confirm the delete and name the count of pages it will ungroup.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Take a page back out of a folder, or reorder pages inside one
ux.finding: A page inside a folder cannot be reordered and cannot be dragged out. Its row is draggable, so dragging it feels like it should work — but folder children are given no reorder target, and dropping one onto the ungrouped list below moves it in the engine while the row stays exactly where it was, because the list filters folder members out. The only real exit is an 8px close icon that appears beside the row.
ux.evidence: PageFolder.tsx:280-297 renders child PageRow with draggable and no onReorderDrop; PageList.tsx:298-302 filters the root list to pages not in a folder; PageFolder.tsx:265-277 the tiny 'Remove from folder' IconButton. Searched: 'onReorderDrop', 'onPageRemove', 'pageToFolder'.
ux.fix: Make drag do what drag looks like it does: dropping a folder child on the ungrouped list removes it from the folder; dropping it on a sibling reorders within the folder.

ux.screen: Pages panel — Listings vs Page settings
ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: See which pages need SEO work
ux.finding: The same page carries two different SEO scores computed two different ways, and clicking the row is how you get from one to the other. The Listings table scores 100 minus penalties; the settings modal that the row opens scores 0 upwards on a different rule set, and it counts the page name as a set title where the table penalises exactly that. A user who clicks a row reading 85 lands on a panel reading something else with no explanation.
ux.evidence: components/SearchListingsTable.tsx:39-61 buildRows (penalty model, -40 no description, -15 title falls back to name, -25 duplicate title, -20 noIndex); utils/seoScore.ts:28-39 calculateSeoScore (additive model); page-settings/usePageSettings.ts:107 pre-fills seoTitle from page.name so the drawer never sees the fallback the table penalises. Searched: 'seoScore', 'buildRows', 'calculateSeoScore'.
ux.fix: One score, one definition, computed in one place and shown identically in both surfaces.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Widen the listings table to read it
ux.finding: 'Open full listings' closes the full listings. The link is wired to the panel's expand TOGGLE, so on a panel already widened to its 700px state — which is exactly the state a user reading a four-column table would be in — clicking it collapses the panel back to 280px. The link's label says only one of the two things it does.
ux.evidence: PagesTab.tsx:260 SearchListingsTable onOpenFull={onExpandToggle}; sidebar/LeftSidebar.tsx:381 onExpandToggle flips a boolean; :586-587 that boolean chooses 700 or the default width. Searched: 'onOpenFull', 'onExpandToggle', 'isExpanded'.
ux.fix: Expand, do not toggle. Hide or relabel the link once the panel is already at full width.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Set the image that shows when this page is shared
ux.finding: The share image is a bare URL text box in a product with a full media library. There is no 'choose from library', no upload, no validation and no broken-image state — the preview simply shows nothing if the URL is wrong, because the preview image has an empty alt. The user has to leave the panel, upload the image somewhere, find its address and paste it back.
ux.evidence: page-settings/SocialTab.tsx:69-79 the Image URL field is a plain type=url TextInput; :28-30 the preview img has alt="" and no error handling; the media library is reachable from the shell but not from here. Searched: 'ogImage', 'onOpenLibrary', 'MediaPicker', 'upload'.
ux.fix: Put the media library behind this field, with an upload fallback and a visible failed-to-load state.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Look at a page's SEO settings without changing anything
ux.finding: Opening page settings quietly freezes the search title. The Title field is pre-filled with the page name when no custom title exists, presented exactly like a value the user set — and the first save writes it as a real, stored title. From then on the search result no longer follows the page name: rename the page and Google keeps showing the old one, with nothing anywhere saying the field had been a default.
ux.evidence: page-settings/usePageSettings.ts:107 (seoTitle: page.seo?.metaTitle ?? page.name); :275 save writes metaTitle: seoTitle || undefined; the drawer autosaves 500ms after any change (PageSettingsDrawer.tsx:41-45). Searched: 'metaTitle', 'getPersistedState', 'seoTitle'.
ux.fix: Show the derived title as a placeholder, not a value, and only persist what the user typed.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Keep the SEO data an import or a template gave my page
ux.finding: Saving page settings silently deletes the SEO fields this form does not draw. The save replaces the whole SEO object with the seven fields the two tabs collect, and the engine merges only one level above that — so a canonical URL, JSON-LD structured data, or any Twitter card fields that arrived with an import are gone the first time a user edits a meta description. None of those six fields has an input anywhere in the product, so the user cannot even see what was lost.
ux.evidence: page-settings/usePageSettings.ts:274-282 writes a fresh seo object; engine/elements/manager/PageManager.ts:156 page.settings = { ...page.settings, ...data.settings } (shallow, so settings.seo is replaced whole); shared/types/project.ts:233-247 declares twitterCard, twitterTitle, twitterDescription, twitterImage, canonicalUrl, structuredData. Searched: 'canonicalUrl', 'structuredData', 'twitterCard', 'settings.seo'. (Confirms prior claim MOD-B-26 and W-F-17.)
ux.fix: Merge the SEO object instead of replacing it, and give the six orphan fields either an input or a deletion.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Understand what 'Hidden' does to my page
ux.finding: The visibility control says two opposite things about the same choice, at the same time, one line apart. Choosing Hidden renders 'Not published. Hidden pages are left out of the deploy' immediately above 'Page is not linked in menus but reachable via direct URL.' A user reading top to bottom cannot tell whether their hidden page exists on the internet. The password option carries the same contradiction.
ux.evidence: page-settings/AdvancedTab.tsx:49-56 (the 'left out of the deploy' helper, shown whenever visibility !== 'live') and :57-61 (the unconditional per-option helper). Searched: 'visibility', 'HelperText', 'hidden'. (Confirms prior claim MOD-B-17.)
ux.fix: One sentence per option, describing what the product actually does today.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: See and manage the pages my content collection generates
ux.finding: RE-VERIFIED the prior 'unwired' claim and it is stale: dynamic pages ARE reachable — the view is spelled 'dynamic-pages', the Content panel passes the door and renders the screen. The real gap is on this module's side: a collection with a pattern like /menu/{slug} generates one published page per record and NONE of them appear in Pages, in the Structure tree, or in the Listings table — so a site can publish forty URLs the page manager has never heard of. The page that serves as their template is typed as a free-text export path in a setup modal, not picked from the pages the user actually has, so nothing connects the two modules at all.
ux.evidence: content/useContentPanel.ts:28 declares { kind: 'dynamic-pages' }; content/ContentTab.tsx:256 passes onOpenDynamicPages and :299 renders DynamicPagesView; content/ContentViews.tsx:600-680 the screen itself. On the Pages side, usePages.ts:103 lists only composer.elements.getAllPages(); shell/modals/CMSCollectionSetupModal.tsx:440 collects pageTemplatePath as free text ('Template page path — blog/_template/index.html'). Searched: 'dynamic-pages', 'dynamicPages', 'DYNAMIC_PAGE', 'pageSlugPattern', 'pageTemplatePath'.
ux.fix: List generated routes in the Pages tree as a read-only group under their collection, mark the template page in the list, and make the template a picker over real pages rather than a typed filename.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Jump to a page with the keyboard
ux.finding: Pressing Cmd-K with the Pages panel open opens two palettes on top of each other. The shell binds Cmd-K for the global command palette on the document, the Pages panel binds its own page-jump palette on the window, and a keydown reaches both — the panel prevents the browser default but never stops the event, so both handlers run. The panel also advertises the chord with a key cap in its header, which is the one place a user would learn to press it.
ux.evidence: shell/StudioHeader.tsx:257-272 (document listener, toggles the command palette); PagesTab.tsx:125-137 (window listener, toggles PageCommandPalette; preventDefault only, no stopPropagation); PagesTab.tsx:222-232 renders the Cmd-K key cap in the panel header. Searched: 'metaKey', '"k"', 'CommandPalette', 'setCmdOpen'.
ux.fix: One Cmd-K. If the Pages panel is open, the global palette should scope itself to pages rather than a second overlay opening behind it.

ux.screen: Pages panel — after a failed load
ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Open a site when the server is unreachable
ux.finding: When the project fails to load, the Pages panel confidently shows a one-page site the editor invented. The shell falls back to browser storage and, failing that, creates a page called 'Home' — and the panel then draws 'This site has one page.' with a '+ Add page' invitation over a site that has ten pages on the server. The panel has no degraded state of its own: its load-error body only appears if reading the page list throws, which a network failure never does.
ux.evidence: shell/hooks/useComposerInit.ts:280-330 the load .catch, :339-381 loadFromLocalStorage which creates a page via getDefaultPageName when nothing is stored; PageList.tsx:334-345 the one-page note; usePages.ts:127-129 loadError is set only when composer.elements.getAllPages() throws; :438 loading = !loaded && !loadError. Searched: 'loadError', 'PROJECT_LOADED', 'hasProjectLoaded', 'onLoadError'.
ux.fix: Let the panel hear the load failure directly and say it: 'Couldn't reach your site — these pages are local only', with editing held back until the real project arrives or the user chooses to work offline.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Switch to another page
ux.finding: Switching pages leaves the inspector editing an element on the page you just left. Nothing clears the canvas selection when the active page changes, so the right-hand panel keeps showing size, style and link controls for something that is no longer on screen, and edits made there land on the invisible element. Deleting a page has the same shape: its elements are removed from the registry without the selection being cleared.
ux.evidence: engine/elements/manager/PageManager.ts:222-236 setActivePage emits page:activated and PAGE_CHANGED; :254-278 deletePage removes descendants from the registry; engine/SelectionManager.ts subscribes to no events and its clear() (:103) is called by nothing on a page switch. Searched: 'clearSelection', 'SELECTION_CLEARED', 'PAGE_CHANGED', 'setActivePage'. (Confirms prior claim MOD-B-20.)
ux.fix: Clear the selection on page activation and on the delete of the page that owns it.

ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Get back a page I deleted five minutes ago
ux.finding: There is no recently-deleted anywhere. Undo is the only recovery, and it is the single editor-wide history stack — so a page deleted and then followed by three canvas edits needs four undos, which also throw away the three edits. The confirm dialog names Cmd-Z as the way back and it is honest only for the very next action.
ux.evidence: PagesTab.tsx:329 and :345-347 name Cmd-Z as the only recovery; usePages.ts:279-289 the toast's Undo calls composer.history.undo(); engine/HistoryManager.ts:129 records every PROJECT_CHANGED onto one stack. Searched: 'trash', 'recentlyDeleted', 'restorePage', 'archive', 'deletedPages' — none exist under editor/ or engine/.
ux.fix: Keep deleted pages recoverable for a session independently of the undo stack, reachable from the Pages panel.

ux.screen: Pages panel — row and context menu
ux.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
ux.task: Work through my pages from the keyboard
ux.finding: Page management is mouse work with one exception. A focused row answers Enter (open), F2 (rename) and Space (select) and nothing else — no Delete key, no duplicate, no way to open settings, no shortcut for a new page. The context menu draws no shortcut hints at all, and the two chords its own source claims still work do not: nothing binds a duplicate chord anywhere, and Cmd-comma opens SITE settings, not page settings.
ux.evidence: PageRow.tsx:194-205 (Enter / F2 / Space only); PageContextMenu.tsx:89-90 the comment claiming 'F2 / Cmd-D / Cmd-comma'; shell/hooks/useEditorShortcuts.ts:119-122 Cmd-comma calls openSiteSettings. Searched: 'key === "d"', "key === 'd'", 'key.toLowerCase() === \"d\"', 'duplicatePage', 'key === ","' — no duplicate binding exists anywhere in editor/.
ux.fix: Bind the row actions the menu offers, and print the chords on the menu items so they are discoverable.

ux.task: Write a share title that will not be truncated
ux.finding: The character counters on the Social tab are decorative. They print length over 60 and length over 160 in one fixed muted colour and enforce nothing — the field accepts 300 characters with the counter looking exactly as calm as at 20. The SEO tab one click away hard-limits its equivalent fields at the same numbers, so the same counter means two different things in the same modal.
ux.evidence: page-settings/SocialTab.tsx:44 and :59 render the counters with a fixed colour and the inputs have no maxLength and no slice; page-settings/SeoTab.tsx:158 and :208 slice their values at 60 and 160 and colour the counter by range. Searched: 'maxLength', 'slice(0', 'length}/'.
ux.fix: Make the two tabs behave the same way — warn at the limit or enforce it, but not one each.

ux.task: Understand how my pages relate to each other
ux.finding: The Structure view is read-only and leads nowhere. It draws the route tree and lets you select a page, but offers none of the actions the tree one click away has — no rename, no settings, no reorder, no context menu — and selecting a page leaves the user standing in Structure with the canvas silently changed behind the panel. Segments with no page of their own are shown as '(no page)' with no way to create one there, which is the one action that gap invites.
ux.evidence: components/SiteStructureTree.tsx:42-69 Branch renders a name button and a path, nothing else; :50 onSelectPage only; PagesTab.tsx:238-239 wires it to selectPage and a back link. Searched: 'SiteStructureTree', 'buildRouteTree', 'onSelectPage'.
ux.fix: Carry the same row actions into Structure, and make a '(no page)' segment offer to create the missing page at that route.

summary.purpose: Pages & routing — create, name, order, address and configure the individual screens of a site, and decide which of them actually ship.
summary.finding: PURPOSE: Pages & Routing is where a site's individual screens are created, named, ordered, addressed (slug/route), configured for search and sharing, and decided in or out of a publish. PRIMARY TASKS: add a page (blank, from a template, or duplicated); rename it; give it a URL; set which page is the homepage; order and group pages; open a page to edit it; configure per-page SEO, social and visibility; delete a page. ENTRY POINTS: the rail's Pages tool (bare 'P'), the always-visible page tab bar under the canvas, the Templates panel's new-page flow, the Templates success modal (which asks the composer to open page settings), the Listings and Structure views inside the panel, the shell command palette, and a deep link. EXIT POINTS: the panel header's close, Escape or scrim on the settings modal, the '< Pages' back links from Listings and Structure, and switching rail tools. HANDS OFF TO: Publish (which counts and ships exactly the pages this module marks live), Export (which resolves the homepage, the file names and every internal link from this module's data), Settings > Redirects (named in copy but never linked), Templates (new page from template), Media (needed for the social image but not reachable from it), and the Inspector's Link section (the only place a page becomes a clickable link). RECEIVES FROM: Templates (creates pages), the Content/CMS module (generates pages this panel cannot see), the shell's project load (and its fallback, which can invent a page), History (undo restores deleted pages), and the collaboration/dirty-state layer (the unsaved dot on a row). THE STRUCTURAL GAP: this module manages pages as records and not as a site — it can create a page but not make it reachable, it labels a page Draft that the deploy ships, and the homepage is decided by list position when nobody has chosen one.
summary.evidence: Read end to end: sidebar/tabs/pages/ (PagesTab.tsx, usePages.ts, useFolders.ts, useBulkSelect.ts, components/*, page-settings/*, utils/*), engine/elements/manager/PageManager.ts, engine/routing/PageRouter.ts, shell/PageTabBar.tsx, sidebar/TabRouter.tsx, rail/tabsConfig.ts, export/ExportEngine.ts (isPageLive, resolveIndexPage, link rewriting), publish/usePublishSnapshot.ts, content/ContentTab.tsx + ContentViews.tsx (dynamic-pages), settings/screens/RedirectsScreen.tsx, inspector/sections/LinkSection.tsx, blocks/Sections/Navbar.tsx.
